goode.trailheadDirection: South-southeast via Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) descent, then east up North Fork Bridge Creek
goode.routeDescription: Grade III-IV alpine rock route with 5.4-5.5 climbing. Approach via 10-mile PCT descent to Bridge Creek junction, then 3-4 miles up North Fork Bridge Creek to base camp. Route ascends the Northeast Buttress with glacier travel, scrambling (3rd-4th class), and rock pitches up to 5.5. Total trip: 3-4 days recommended. Note: Mount Goode has no documented 'Northwest Buttress' route; this is the main and most popular alpine route.
goode.accessInfo: Backcountry permit required ($10 + $6 fee) from North Cascades Visitor Center in Marblemount. Best climbing season: late July through September (early season has dangerous water crossings at Grizzly Creek and North Fork Bridge Creek). Located within North Cascades National Park. Large paved parking available at trailhead.
goode.notes: Research confirmed Northeast Buttress is the main/documented route; no Northwest Buttress variant exists. Excellent approach beta available from multiple sources.
